what: As a full-bleed photo/video panel enters from below the screen, it starts at the middle half width (clip inset 25%, corners .5rem) and opens to fill the screen, tied to scroll, until the panel’s top edge touches the top of the screen (curve cubic-bezier(.47,0,.745,.715)). With the same progress, the corner arcs of the box inside the panel come in from outside, 20rem horizontally and 40rem vertically for the bottom two, and attach to the corners to form a frame

options.from: Initial share cropped from left and right (%), default 25
options.round: Initial corner radius (px) — becomes 0 as it opens, default 8
options.ease: Curve (four cubic-bezier numbers or a GSAP name), default 0.47,0,0.745,0.715
options.--fx-dx: Horizontal distance between the ear arcs (via style), default 20rem
options.--fx-dy: Vertical distance between the two lower ear arcs (via style, negative means up), default -40rem
options.--fx-size: Corner arc side length (via style), default 2.6rem
options.[data-fx-part=corner]: Corner arc (optional) — data-key holds tl, tr, bl or br, with one SVG arc curving to the top left inside. Position is relative to the nearest positioned ancestor (usually the center square box)

use: …
note: The original runs on CSS animation-timeline: view(). The part runs the same range with ScrollTrigger scrub so it also works inside inner scroll panels. The panel is sticky and the outer cell is more than one screen tall.
